narration.full_text: Namaste students! It's time to test your understanding of control and coordination. Get ready to challenge yourselves with some thought-provoking questions. Let's begin! First question: Write names of hormones secreted by pituitary gland and adrenal gland. State their functions in the body. And, explain feedback mechanism for regulation of hormonal secretion with the help of one example. Here's the answer. Pituitary gland secretes growth hormone, which regulates growth and development of the body. Adrenal gland secretes adrenaline hormone, which creates stress in our body. The timing and amount of hormones released by various glands is controlled by a feedback mechanism. For example, if blood sugar levels rise, the pancreas secretes more insulin. As blood sugar falls, insulin secretion is reduced automatically. Next question: What happens at the synapse between two neurons? Take a moment to think about it. And the answer is: At the synapse, the electrical impulse generated at the dendrites of one neuron is passed on to the dendrite of another neuron in the form of chemicals by the axon ending of the first neuron. Moving on to the next question: Design an experiment to demonstrate hydrotropism. Consider how you would set this up. Here's the explanation: Hydrotropism can be demonstrated with germinating seedlings grown on the ground. Separate the soil around the roots with a polythene partition. Keep one side moist and the other dry. The radicle will initially grow downwards, then bend towards the moist soil, showing the roots' movement towards water. And finally, the last question: Why is the use of iodised salt advisable? Think about the role of iodine in the body. The answer is: Iodine is necessary to make thyroxine hormone, which regulates carbohydrate, protein, and fat metabolism in the body. This ensures the best balance for growth. Great job, everyone! I hope you learned a lot from this quiz.

visual_beats.description: Question: 21. (i) Write names of hormones secreted by pituitary gland and adrenal gland. State their functions in the body. (ii) Explain feedback mechanism for regulation of hormonal secretion with the help of one example.

Answer: (i) Pituitary gland secretes growth hormone. It regulates growth and development of the body. Adrenal gland secretes adrenaline hormone. It creates stress in our body. (ii) The timing and amount of hormones released by various glands is controlled by feedback mechanism which is inbuilt in our body, e.g. if sugar level in blood rises too high, it is detected by cells of pancreas which respond by producing and secreting more insulin into blood. As blood sugar falls to certain level, the secretion of insulin is reduced automatically.
Question: 22. What happens at the synapse between two neurons?
Answer: At synapse the electrical impulse generated at dendrites of a neuron is passed on to dendrite of another neuron in the form of chemicals by axon ending of the first neuron.
Question: 23. Design an experiment to demonstrate hydrotropism.

Answer: Hydrotropism can be demonstrated with any germinating seedlings, which are allowed to grow on ground. The soil around the roots is separated by a polythene partition. The left side is kept moist and the right side dry. The radicle at first grows in a downward direction and after sometime the roots bend towards the moist soil. This is due to movement of the germinating roots to water.
Question: 24. Why is use of iodised salt advisable?
Answer: Iodine is necessary to make thyroxine hormone which regulates carbohydrates, protein and fat metabolism in the body so as to provide the best balance for growth.
